stories.who: His own permission to give khutbahs
stories.point: The minbar is a serious trust, granted only after years of study and supervised khutbahs.

stories.who: Quraysh searching for a flaw in the Prophet
stories.point: His impeccable ethics left his enemies nothing to use, and the whole message rested on that.

contemporary: Portrayals of Islam as a violent faith
Many separate Jumuahs in one city and Muslim disorganization
Domestic violence in the community
takeaways: Treat non-Muslims who do not fight you with your best conduct, beyond mere fairness.
Anyone giving a khutbah should teach who Allah is, purification, the laws and the wisdom to apply them.
Pardon your spouse and children completely, letting go of petty grievances.
Pardon others before you ask Allah to pardon you.
Study the Prophet's consistency of character and try to follow it.

47:19.ar: فَٱعۡلَمۡ أَنَّهُۥ لَآ إِلَٰهَ إِلَّا ٱللَّهُ وَٱسۡتَغۡفِرۡ لِذَنۢبِكَ وَلِلۡمُؤۡمِنِينَ وَٱلۡمُؤۡمِنَٰتِۗ وَٱللَّهُ يَعۡلَمُ مُتَقَلَّبَكُمۡ وَمَثۡوَىٰكُمۡ
47:19.en: So know (O Muhammad) that there is no Allah save Allah, and ask forgiveness for thy sin and for believing men and believing women. Allah knoweth (both) your place of turmoil and your place of rest

47:36.ar: إِنَّمَا ٱلۡحَيَوٰةُ ٱلدُّنۡيَا لَعِبࣱ وَلَهۡوࣱۚ وَإِن تُؤۡمِنُواْ وَتَتَّقُواْ يُؤۡتِكُمۡ أُجُورَكُمۡ وَلَا يَسۡـَٔلۡكُمۡ أَمۡوَٰلَكُمۡ
47:36.en: The life of the world is but a sport and a pastime. And if ye believe and ward off (evil). He will give you your wages, and will not ask of you your wordly wealth

47:37.ar: إِن يَسۡـَٔلۡكُمُوهَا فَيُحۡفِكُمۡ تَبۡخَلُواْ وَيُخۡرِجۡ أَضۡغَٰنَكُمۡ
47:37.en: If He should ask it of you and importune you, ye would hoard it, and He would bring to light your (secret) hates

47:38.ar: هَٰٓأَنتُمۡ هَٰٓؤُلَآءِ تُدۡعَوۡنَ لِتُنفِقُواْ فِي سَبِيلِ ٱللَّهِ فَمِنكُم مَّن يَبۡخَلُۖ وَمَن يَبۡخَلۡ فَإِنَّمَا يَبۡخَلُ عَن نَّفۡسِهِۦۚ وَٱللَّهُ ٱلۡغَنِيُّ وَأَنتُمُ ٱلۡفُقَرَآءُۚ وَإِن تَتَوَلَّوۡاْ يَسۡتَبۡدِلۡ قَوۡمًا غَيۡرَكُمۡ ثُمَّ لَا يَكُونُوٓاْ أَمۡثَٰلَكُم
47:38.en: Lo! ye are those who are called to spend in the way of Allah, yet among you there are some who hoard. And as for him who hoardeth, he hoardeth only from his soul. And Allah is the Rich, and ye are the poor. And if ye turn away He will exchange you for some other folk, and they will not be the likes of you

48:18.ar: ۞لَّقَدۡ رَضِيَ ٱللَّهُ عَنِ ٱلۡمُؤۡمِنِينَ إِذۡ يُبَايِعُونَكَ تَحۡتَ ٱلشَّجَرَةِ فَعَلِمَ مَا فِي قُلُوبِهِمۡ فَأَنزَلَ ٱلسَّكِينَةَ عَلَيۡهِمۡ وَأَثَٰبَهُمۡ فَتۡحࣰ ا قَرِيبࣰ ا
48:18.en: Allah was well pleased with the believers when they swore allegiance unto thee beneath the tree, and He knew what was in their hearts, and He sent down peace of reassurance on them, and hath rewarded them with a near victory

48:29.ar: مُّحَمَّدࣱ رَّسُولُ ٱللَّهِۚ وَٱلَّذِينَ مَعَهُۥٓ أَشِدَّآءُ عَلَى ٱلۡكُفَّارِ رُحَمَآءُ بَيۡنَهُمۡۖ تَرَىٰهُمۡ رُكَّعࣰ ا سُجَّدࣰ ا يَبۡتَغُونَ فَضۡلࣰ ا مِّنَ ٱللَّهِ وَرِضۡوَٰنࣰ اۖ سِيمَاهُمۡ فِي وُجُوهِهِم مِّنۡ أَثَرِ ٱلسُّجُودِۚ ذَٰلِكَ مَثَلُهُمۡ فِي ٱلتَّوۡرَىٰةِۚ وَمَثَلُهُمۡ فِي ٱلۡإِنجِيلِ كَزَرۡعٍ أَخۡرَجَ شَطۡـَٔهُۥ فَـَٔازَرَهُۥ فَٱسۡتَغۡلَظَ فَٱسۡتَوَىٰ عَلَىٰ سُوقِهِۦ يُعۡجِبُ ٱلزُّرَّاعَ لِيَغِيظَ بِهِمُ ٱلۡكُفَّارَۗ وَعَدَ ٱللَّهُ ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُواْ وَعَمِلُواْ ٱلصَّٰلِحَٰتِ مِنۡهُم مَّغۡفِرَةࣰ وَأَجۡرًا عَظِيمَۢا
48:29.en: Muhammad is the messenger of Allah. And those with him are hard against the disbelievers and merciful among themselves. Thou (O Muhammad) seest them bowing and falling prostrate (in worship), seeking bounty from Allah and (His) acceptance. The mark of them is on their foreheads from the traces of prostration. Such is their likeness in the Torah and their likeness in the Gospel - like as sown corn that sendeth forth its shoot and strengtheneth it and riseth firm upon its stalk, delighting the sowers - that He may enrage the disbelievers with (the sight of) them. Allah hath promised, unto such of them as believe and do good works, forgiveness and immense reward

49:13.ar: يَٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلنَّاسُ إِنَّا خَلَقۡنَٰكُم مِّن ذَكَرࣲ وَأُنثَىٰ وَجَعَلۡنَٰكُمۡ شُعُوبࣰ ا وَقَبَآئِلَ لِتَعَارَفُوٓاْۚ إِنَّ أَكۡرَمَكُمۡ عِندَ ٱللَّهِ أَتۡقَىٰكُمۡۚ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ عَلِيمٌ خَبِيرࣱ‏
49:13.en: O mankind! Lo! We have created you male and female, and have made you nations and tribes that ye may know one another. Lo! the noblest of you, in the sight of Allah, is the best in conduct. Lo! Allah is Knower, Aware

50:22.ar: لَّقَدۡ كُنتَ فِي غَفۡلَةࣲ مِّنۡ هَٰذَا فَكَشَفۡنَا عَنكَ غِطَآءَكَ فَبَصَرُكَ ٱلۡيَوۡمَ حَدِيدࣱ‏
50:22.en: (And unto the evil-doer it is said): Thou wast in heedlessness of this. Now We have removed from thee thy covering, and piercing is thy sight this day

52:48.ar: وَٱصۡبِرۡ لِحُكۡمِ رَبِّكَ فَإِنَّكَ بِأَعۡيُنِنَاۖ وَسَبِّحۡ بِحَمۡدِ رَبِّكَ حِينَ تَقُومُ
52:48.en: So wait patiently (O Muhammad) for thy Lord's decree, for surely thou art in Our sight; and hymn the praise of thy Lord when thou uprisest

52:49.en: And in the night-time also hymn His praise, and at the setting of the stars

gzLT1lgqaCA.speaker: adnan
gzLT1lgqaCA.speaker_note: leads the nightly reflections and refers to his Sunday-night tafsir of these surahs
gzLT1lgqaCA.title: Ramadan 2023, Night 25: Quranic Reflections (Muhammad to Al-Najm)
gzLT1lgqaCA.one_line: Tawhid as knowledge, the hidden stinginess Allah spares us, the companions as a cultivated seed, diversity by design, the veil lifted, and patience under Allah's eyes.
gzLT1lgqaCA.summary: He frames the cluster from Muhammad to al-Hujurat as about the Prophet, and the next, from Qaf to al-Hadid, as a series of choices. 'Know that there is no god but Allah' commands knowledge, not recitation: tawhid is learned from people with sacred knowledge, not inherited. Allah does not demand all our wealth because that would expose the stinginess and hidden grudges in us, so He commands only what we can bear, though a command we do not understand still binds us. The companions described at the end of al-Fath were a seed the Prophet watered for 23 years; because he mentored them deeply, Islam spread, and every Muslim's function is to pass the deen on so knowledge widens instead of dying out. Al-Hujurat 49:13 makes human difference a design for getting to know one another, and since rank depends on taqwa, which no one can measure, no human can say who is better. Qaf's lifted veil gives perfect sight on the Day it no longer helps, so reflect on death now. Al-Tur tells the Prophet, who had no guarantee of success, to persevere because he is under Allah's eyes, and to glorify Allah whenever he takes a stand.

outline.heading: Opening
Muhammad to al-Hujurat: the Prophet's cluster
outline.gist: These surahs cover his rights, sacrifices, our relationship with him, his role as model and the manners owed to him.

outline.heading: Qaf to al-Hadid: a cluster of choices
outline.gist: Each surah sets two paths side by side: righteousness or falsehood, purpose or aimlessness, guidance or none, knowledge or whims.

outline.heading: Spirituality and materialism in balance
outline.gist: Two surahs on blessings do not ask you to choose one but to balance both.

outline.heading: Know that there is no god but Allah
outline.gist: Tawhid is not a word we inherit but something learned and rooted in knowledge; embracing ignorance harms oneself and others.

outline.heading: Allah knows your ups and downs
outline.gist: Your movement and your resting place stand for how life lifts and drops us, and where we finally end up.

outline.heading: Know it, not just say it
outline.gist: The verse says know, not say, so we need people with sacred knowledge to teach its meaning and practice.

outline.heading: He does not ask you for all your wealth
outline.gist: This life is play and distraction; believe and be mindful and Allah gives your reward without demanding everything you own.

outline.heading: A demand that would expose your hidden grudges
outline.gist: Asked for all of it, we would refuse; Allah only commands what serves us, out of His mercy.

outline.heading: Hidden diseases that go unexposed
outline.gist: Most of us never face the test that would reveal our hidden bigotry, hatred and stinginess, but they are still there.

outline.heading: A command you dislike is still a command
outline.gist: Not agreeing with a command does not remove accountability; mercifully, Allah asks nothing that would break us.

outline.heading: Those who stood by him are honoured too
outline.gist: Not only the Prophet's legacy and sacrifice are sacred but also the companions he died pleased with.

outline.heading: The pledge under the tree
outline.gist: On the way to umrah, believing Uthman had been killed, they pledged to fight to the death, and Allah declared His pleasure with them.

outline.heading: The mark of prostration on their faces
outline.gist: How a person spends their time shows in the face; the companions' closeness to Allah was visible.

outline.heading: A seed that grows strong
outline.gist: Their likeness in the Torah and Gospel is a seed tended until it stands on its own, delighting the sowers and angering disbelievers.

outline.heading: Twenty-three years of tending people
outline.gist: The Prophet taught, empowered and mentored those around him until they could carry Islam to the world.

outline.heading: Passing it on, generation to generation
outline.gist: Had his investment been shallow, his teachings would have dissolved over the centuries; mentoring is the spirit of the faith.

outline.heading: Every Muslim's function
outline.gist: Wherever we live, our job is to make sure the next generation can embrace, practise, teach and spread Islam as well as we do.

outline.heading: Knowledge should widen like a pyramid
outline.gist: When it narrows instead, it is only a matter of time; the loss of knowledge is a sign of the Hour we can actually prevent.

outline.heading: A verse with no parallel
outline.gist: He doubts any other scripture contains a verse like it.

outline.heading: Peoples and tribes so you may know one another
outline.gist: From one pair, Allah made peoples and communities, defined by background rather than race.

outline.heading: Why 'know one another'
outline.gist: Allah chose acquaintance, not guiding each other or proving who is right: go and explore other ways of life.

outline.heading: Beauty in diversity, one book for all
outline.gist: Cultures, languages and customs differ, yet the Quran suits every one of them and we can learn from each other.

outline.heading: Taqwa cannot be measured
outline.gist: Prayers in congregation and fasts can be counted, but taqwa is in the heart; we do not know our own, let alone others'.

outline.heading: No one can say who is better
outline.gist: If rank rests on taqwa, humans by definition cannot rank each other; we are diverse by design, not so others become like us.

outline.heading: Knowing and Aware: what is inside
outline.gist: Khabir is used for knowing what lies within and is hidden from the senses, beyond Allah's general knowledge.

outline.heading: Qaf: the choice between two paths
outline.gist: The surahs keep putting a choice before you; make the right one and move to the next surah.

outline.heading: You were heedless of this
outline.gist: After walking through creation, death and resurrection, the verse confronts us with our heedlessness.

outline.heading: We avoid thinking about death
outline.gist: Death and what follows are uncomfortable, so we avoid them; then the veil is lifted and sight becomes sharp as iron.

outline.heading: Clarity that comes too late
outline.gist: On that Day all doubts vanish, but clarity then is worthless; only clarity in this life counts.

outline.heading: If only a little earlier
outline.gist: A little reflection before would have guided choices; that Day no one has a question left.

outline.heading: Interlude
Be patient for your Lord's decision
outline.gist: The Prophet was never guaranteed his work would succeed; he was told to persevere until Allah's ruling came.

outline.heading: The prophets' stories mostly ended hard
outline.gist: Isa and Yahya were threatened or killed and Ibrahim was driven from his home; few examples promised success.

outline.heading: You are under Our eyes
outline.gist: Like the Arab expression of giving someone your eyes, it means constant care and protection.

outline.heading: His watch never stops
outline.gist: This applies to all who do the Prophet's work; if you stop feeling it, your sensitivity faded, not His care.

outline.heading: Glorify Him whenever you take a stand
outline.gist: Rising here means taking a stand, a mentality rather than a posture; praise Allah as you do.

outline.heading: At night and as the stars fade
outline.gist: Keep glorifying Him through the night and after dawn, the root of staying after Fajr until sunrise.

outline.heading: Outro

themes.label: Seeking knowledge, learning and scholars
themes.note: La ilaha illa Allah must be known and learned from people of sacred knowledge, not just said or inherited.

themes.label: Selfishness, greed of the soul (shuhh) and selflessness
themes.note: A demand for all our wealth would expose hidden stinginess and grudges; Allah mercifully asks only what we can bear.

themes.label: The companions and the early generations
themes.note: The companions are honoured with the Prophet; their devotion showed on their faces and they grew like a tended seed.

themes.label: Mentoring and passing the deen to the next generation
themes.note: The Prophet invested 23 years in people; every Muslim's function is to pass the deen on so knowledge widens.

themes.label: Human equality and racism
themes.note: Human diversity is by design so we know one another, and only Allah can rank people by taqwa.

themes.label: Taqwa and God-consciousness
themes.note: Taqwa is in the heart, unmeasurable even to oneself, and known only to the One who knows what is within.

themes.label: The Hereafter: resurrection, judgment, paradise, hellfire
themes.note: The veil lifted on the Day brings clarity that no longer helps, so reflect on death and accountability now.

themes.label: Patience (sabr) and perseverance
themes.note: Persevere without a guaranteed outcome, knowing you are always under Allah's eyes.

themes.label: Spirituality, khushoo and the inner life
themes.note: Glorify Allah whenever you take a stand, through the night and as dawn breaks.

hadith.gist: Among the signs of the Hour is that knowledge will be taken away.
The Prophet pointed to his chest and said that taqwa is here.

maxims: Tawhid is learned, not inherited
Knowledge should spread like a widening pyramid
Diverse by design
No human can tell who is better
If you stop feeling His watch, your sensitivity faded
Rising to glorify Him means taking a stand

stories.who: The pledge under the tree at Hudaybiyyah
stories.point: Their readiness to die with the Prophet earned Allah's declared pleasure.
Deep, patient investment in people is why Islam outlived him.
Prophets persevered though many of their stories ended in hardship; success was never promised.

takeaways: Learn the meaning of la ilaha illa Allah from people of knowledge rather than just repeating it.
Invest real time mentoring and teaching the next generation.
Never rank people by race, background or visible acts; learn from those who differ from you.
Reflect on death and the Hereafter now, while clarity can still change your choices.
Keep doing the right work without a guaranteed outcome, trusting that you are under Allah's care.

89:23.ar: وَجِاْيٓءَ يَوۡمَئِذِۭ بِجَهَنَّمَۚ يَوۡمَئِذࣲ يَتَذَكَّرُ ٱلۡإِنسَٰنُ وَأَنَّىٰ لَهُ ٱلذِّكۡرَىٰ
89:23.en: And hell is brought near that day; on that day man will remember, but how will the remembrance (then avail him)

54:7.ar: خُشَّعًا أَبۡصَٰرُهُمۡ يَخۡرُجُونَ مِنَ ٱلۡأَجۡدَاثِ كَأَنَّهُمۡ جَرَادࣱ مُّنتَشِرࣱ‏
54:7.en: With downcast eyes, they come forth from the graves as they were locusts spread abroad

54:8.ar: مُّهۡطِعِينَ إِلَى ٱلدَّاعِۖ يَقُولُ ٱلۡكَٰفِرُونَ هَٰذَا يَوۡمٌ عَسِرࣱ‏
54:8.en: Hastening toward the summoner; the disbelievers say: This is a hard day

80:34.en: On the day when a man fleeth from his brother

80:35.en: And his mother and his father

80:36.en: And his wife and his children

80:37.ar: لِكُلِّ ٱمۡرِيࣲٕ مِّنۡهُمۡ يَوۡمَئِذࣲ شَأۡنࣱ يُغۡنِيهِ
80:37.en: Every man that day will have concern enough to make him heedless (of others)

45:28.ar: وَتَرَىٰ كُلَّ أُمَّةࣲ جَاثِيَةࣰۚ كُلُّ أُمَّةࣲ تُدۡعَىٰٓ إِلَىٰ كِتَٰبِهَا ٱلۡيَوۡمَ تُجۡزَوۡنَ مَا كُنتُمۡ تَعۡمَلُونَ
45:28.en: And thou wilt see each nation crouching, each nation summoned to its record. (And it will be said unto them): This day ye are requited what ye used to do

42:45.ar: وَتَرَىٰهُمۡ يُعۡرَضُونَ عَلَيۡهَا خَٰشِعِينَ مِنَ ٱلذُّلِّ يَنظُرُونَ مِن طَرۡفٍ خَفِيࣲّۗ وَقَالَ ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُوٓاْ إِنَّ ٱلۡخَٰسِرِينَ ٱلَّذِينَ خَسِرُوٓاْ أَنفُسَهُمۡ وَأَهۡلِيهِمۡ يَوۡمَ ٱلۡقِيَٰمَةِۗ أَلَآ إِنَّ ٱلظَّٰلِمِينَ فِي عَذَابࣲ مُّقِيمࣲ‏
42:45.en: And thou wilt see them exposed to (the Fire), made humble by disgrace, and looking with veiled eyes. And those who believe will say: Lo! the (eternal) losers are they who lose themselves and their housefolk on the Day of Resurrection. Lo! are not the wrong-doers in perpetual torment

70:11.ar: يُبَصَّرُونَهُمۡۚ يَوَدُّ ٱلۡمُجۡرِمُ لَوۡ يَفۡتَدِي مِنۡ عَذَابِ يَوۡمِئِذِۭ بِبَنِيهِ
70:11.en: Though they will be given sight of them. The guilty man will long to be able to ransom himself from the punishment of that day at the price of his children

70:12.en: And his spouse and his brother

70:13.en: And his kin that harboured him

70:14.ar: وَمَن فِي ٱلۡأَرۡضِ جَمِيعࣰ ا ثُمَّ يُنجِيهِ
70:14.en: And all that are in the earth, if then it might deliver him

70:15.en: But nay! for lo! it is the fire of hell

69:17.ar: وَٱلۡمَلَكُ عَلَىٰٓ أَرۡجَآئِهَاۚ وَيَحۡمِلُ عَرۡشَ رَبِّكَ فَوۡقَهُمۡ يَوۡمَئِذࣲ ثَمَٰنِيَةࣱ‏
69:17.en: And the angels will be on the sides thereof, and eight will uphold the Throne of thy Lord that day, above them

69:18.ar: يَوۡمَئِذࣲ تُعۡرَضُونَ لَا تَخۡفَىٰ مِنكُمۡ خَافِيَةࣱ‏
69:18.en: On that day ye will be exposed; not a secret of you will be hidden

68:42.ar: يَوۡمَ يُكۡشَفُ عَن سَاقࣲ وَيُدۡعَوۡنَ إِلَى ٱلسُّجُودِ فَلَا يَسۡتَطِيعُونَ
68:42.en: On the day when it befalleth in earnest, and they are ordered to prostrate themselves but are not able

68:43.ar: خَٰشِعَةً أَبۡصَٰرُهُمۡ تَرۡهَقُهُمۡ ذِلَّةࣱۖ وَقَدۡ كَانُواْ يُدۡعَوۡنَ إِلَى ٱلسُّجُودِ وَهُمۡ سَٰلِمُونَ
68:43.en: With eyes downcast, abasement stupefying them. And they had been summoned to prostrate themselves while they were yet unhurt

57:13.ar: يَوۡمَ يَقُولُ ٱلۡمُنَٰفِقُونَ وَٱلۡمُنَٰفِقَٰتُ لِلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُواْ ٱنظُرُونَا نَقۡتَبِسۡ مِن نُّورِكُمۡ قِيلَ ٱرۡجِعُواْ وَرَآءَكُمۡ فَٱلۡتَمِسُواْ نُورࣰ اۖ فَضُرِبَ بَيۡنَهُم بِسُورࣲ لَّهُۥ بَابُۢ بَاطِنُهُۥ فِيهِ ٱلرَّحۡمَةُ وَظَٰهِرُهُۥ مِن قِبَلِهِ ٱلۡعَذَابُ
57:13.en: On the day when the hypocritical men and the hypocritical women will say unto those who believe: Look on us that we may borrow from your light! it will be said: Go back and seek for light! Then there will separate them a wall wherein is a gate, the inner side whereof containeth mercy, while the outer side thereof is toward the doom

57:14.ar: يُنَادُونَهُمۡ أَلَمۡ نَكُن مَّعَكُمۡۖ قَالُواْ بَلَىٰ وَلَٰكِنَّكُمۡ فَتَنتُمۡ أَنفُسَكُمۡ وَتَرَبَّصۡتُمۡ وَٱرۡتَبۡتُمۡ وَغَرَّتۡكُمُ ٱلۡأَمَانِيُّ حَتَّىٰ جَآءَ أَمۡرُ ٱللَّهِ وَغَرَّكُم بِٱللَّهِ ٱلۡغَرُورُ
57:14.en: They will cry unto them (saying): Were we not with you? They will say: Yea, verily; but ye tempted one another, and hesitated, and doubted, and vain desires beguiled you till the ordinance of Allah came to pass; and the deceiver deceived you concerning Allah

69:19.ar: فَأَمَّا مَنۡ أُوتِيَ كِتَٰبَهُۥ بِيَمِينِهِۦ فَيَقُولُ هَآؤُمُ ٱقۡرَءُواْ كِتَٰبِيَهۡ
69:19.en: Then, as for him who is given his record in his right hand, he will say: Take, read my book

69:20.en: Surely I knew that I should have to meet my reckoning

69:21.en: Then he will be in blissful state

69:23.en: Whereof the clusters are in easy reach

69:24.ar: كُلُواْ وَٱشۡرَبُواْ هَنِيٓـَٔۢا بِمَآ أَسۡلَفۡتُمۡ فِي ٱلۡأَيَّامِ ٱلۡخَالِيَةِ
69:24.en: (And it will be said unto those therein): Eat and drink at ease for that which ye sent on before you in past days

69:25.ar: وَأَمَّا مَنۡ أُوتِيَ كِتَٰبَهُۥ بِشِمَالِهِۦ فَيَقُولُ يَٰلَيۡتَنِي لَمۡ أُوتَ كِتَٰبِيَهۡ
69:25.en: But as for him who is given his record in his left hand, he will say: Oh, would that I had not been given my book

69:26.en: And knew not what my reckoning

69:27.en: Oh, would that it had been death

69:28.en: My wealth hath not availed me

17:14.ar: ٱقۡرَأۡ كِتَٰبَكَ كَفَىٰ بِنَفۡسِكَ ٱلۡيَوۡمَ عَلَيۡكَ حَسِيبࣰ ا
17:14.en: (And it will be said unto him): Read thy Book. Thy soul sufficeth as reckoner against thee this day

2:218.ar: إِنَّ ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُواْ وَٱلَّذِينَ هَاجَرُواْ وَجَٰهَدُواْ فِي سَبِيلِ ٱللَّهِ أُوْلَٰٓئِكَ يَرۡجُونَ رَحۡمَتَ ٱللَّهِۚ وَٱللَّهُ غَفُورࣱ رَّحِيمࣱ‏
2:218.en: Lo! those who believe, and those who emigrate (to escape the persecution) and strive in the way of Allah, these have hope of Allah's mercy. Allah is Forgiving, Merciful

mNilcNrAp-I.title: Ramadan 2023 Night 27: Tahajjud Program
mNilcNrAp-I.one_line: A guided walk through the Day of Judgment scene by scene, then a call on Laylat al-Qadr to take yourself to account and act on your hope.
mNilcNrAp-I.summary: Night 27 opens, before the prayer, with a guided reflection that walks the congregation through the Day of Judgment scene by scene, pausing between scenes for collective tahlil. Each person is called by name; Allah declares Himself the King and the Compeller and asks where the tyrants of the earth are; people pour from their graves like scattered locusts and flee from their own families (54:7-8, 80:34-37); they stand uncovered while seven kinds of people are shaded by Allah. Nations kneel before their records, the criminal wishes to ransom his children and the whole earth (70:11-16), the Throne is carried and nothing stays hidden (69:17-18), and those who would not prostrate cannot (68:42-43). He brings in the Prophet at his Basin, the hypocrites begging for light over the Fire (57:13-14), the book given in the right or left hand (69:19-30), and finally the moment your own name is called to read your record (17:14). The later reminder between rakaat makes it practical: on Laylat al-Qadr, take yourself to account, since the shrewd person works for what comes after death while the helpless one follows desire and still expects reward; hope belongs to those who act (2:218); and the deeds Allah loves most are the consistent ones.

outline.heading: Called by name before the King
outline.gist: He places the listener at the resurrection: each person called by name, the angels assembled before the King, and Hell brought forward.

outline.heading: Interlude
Allah declares Himself the King
outline.gist: Allah says: I am the King, where are the kings of the earth? I am the Mighty, the Great, the Proud, the Compeller.

outline.heading: Interlude
Out of the graves, fleeing from family
outline.gist: People come out of the graves like scattered locusts, hurrying to the caller (54:7-8), and each flees from brother, mother, father, spouse and children (80:34-37).

outline.heading: Interlude
Raised uncovered
outline.gist: He describes people raised bare and uncovered, and the need for Allah's covering on that Day.

outline.heading: Interlude
Those in Allah's shade
outline.gist: On a day with no shade but His, Allah shades the just ruler, the youth raised in worship, two who love each other for His sake, and the one whose heart is attached to the masjid.

outline.heading: Nations kneeling and the criminal's ransom
outline.gist: Every nation kneels and is called to its record (45:28); people are shown to the Fire, humbled and glancing furtively (42:45); the criminal would give his children, spouse, brother and the whole earth to escape (70:11-16).

outline.heading: Interlude
The Throne carried and nothing hidden
outline.gist: Angels stand at the heavens' edges, eight carry the Throne, and everyone is presented with nothing concealed (69:17-18).

outline.heading: Called to prostrate and unable
outline.gist: On the day the shin is laid bare, those who refused to prostrate while healthy are called to it and cannot (68:42-43).

outline.heading: Interlude
The Prophet at the Basin
outline.gist: He turns to the Prophet at his Basin and the narration in which some are driven away and he is told he does not know what they introduced after him.

outline.heading: Interlude
Over the Fire, the hypocrites beg for light
outline.gist: As people cross above Hell, the hypocrites ask the believers to wait so they can take from their light, and a wall is set between them (57:13-14).

outline.heading: Interlude
The book in the right hand or the left
outline.gist: The one given his book in the right hand rejoices; the one given it in the left wishes he had never received it, his wealth and power gone (69:19-30).

outline.heading: Interlude
Your name is called before al-Jabbar
outline.gist: The angels call a person by name to be presented before the Compeller and told to read his own book, enough as his own reckoner (17:14).

outline.heading: Interlude
Laylat al-Qadr and muhasabah
outline.gist: On a night that may be Laylat al-Qadr he calls for muhasabah, honestly taking stock of oneself.

outline.heading: The shrewd and the helpless
outline.gist: The shrewd one holds himself to account and works for what comes after death; the helpless one follows his desires and still expects Allah to grant his wishes.

outline.heading: Hope that comes with deeds
outline.gist: Those who believe, emigrate and strive are the ones who hope for Allah's mercy (2:218); the companions' hope came with action.

outline.heading: The most beloved deeds are the most consistent
outline.gist: The deeds Allah loves most are those done consistently.

outline.heading: Interlude
Outro

themes.label: The Hereafter: resurrection, judgment, paradise, hellfire
themes.note: A scene-by-scene journey through the Day of Judgment, from the resurrection to receiving one's book.

themes.label: The Names and Attributes of Allah
themes.note: Allah reveals Himself on that Day as al-Malik, al-Aziz, al-Mutakabbir and al-Jabbar.

themes.label: Accountability before Allah and goals
themes.note: Each person is summoned by name and reads his own record.

themes.label: Self-honesty and self-accountability (muhasabah)
themes.note: Taking yourself to account now, as the shrewd person does, instead of living on wishes.

themes.label: Hope, fear and the balance between them
themes.note: Real hope in Allah's mercy is joined to belief and effort.

themes.label: Istiqamah: incorruptibility, steadfastness, moral integrity
themes.note: Consistency is what Allah loves most in deeds.

quran.point: Hell is brought forward on that Day.
People leave the graves like scattered locusts, rushing to the caller.
Each person flees from his own family.
Every nation kneeling, called to its record.
Shown to the Fire, humbled, glancing furtively.
The criminal would ransom his children, spouse and the whole earth.
Eight carry the Throne; nothing hidden on the Day of presentation.
Called to prostrate and unable.
The hypocrites ask for light and are shut out by a wall.
The book in the right hand and the book in the left.
Read your book; you are enough as your own reckoner today.
Those who believe, emigrate and strive are the ones who hope for mercy.

hadith.gist: On the Day of Judgment Allah declares: I am the King, where are the kings of the earth? I am the Compeller, where are the tyrants?
Seven whom Allah shades on the day when there is no shade but His, among them the just ruler, the youth raised in worship and the one whose heart is attached to the masjid.
At the Basin some are driven away and the Prophet is told: you do not know what they introduced after you.
The shrewd one is he who holds himself to account and works for what comes after death; the helpless one follows his desires and pins wishes on Allah.
The most beloved deeds to Allah are the most consistent.

takeaways: Picture the Day of Judgment in detail and let it shape how you spend the remaining nights.
Take yourself to account honestly tonight rather than waiting to be taken to account.
Pair your hope in Allah's mercy with real effort instead of wishful thinking.
Keep up consistent deeds after Ramadan.

41:49.ar: لَّا يَسۡـَٔمُ ٱلۡإِنسَٰنُ مِن دُعَآءِ ٱلۡخَيۡرِ وَإِن مَّسَّهُ ٱلشَّرُّ فَيَـُٔوسࣱ قَنُوطࣱ‏
41:49.en: Man tireth not of praying for good, and if ill toucheth him, then he is disheartened, desperate

41:50.ar: وَلَئِنۡ أَذَقۡنَٰهُ رَحۡمَةࣰ مِّنَّا مِنۢ بَعۡدِ ضَرَّآءَ مَسَّتۡهُ لَيَقُولَنَّ هَٰذَا لِي وَمَآ أَظُنُّ ٱلسَّاعَةَ قَآئِمَةࣰ وَلَئِن رُّجِعۡتُ إِلَىٰ رَبِّيٓ إِنَّ لِي عِندَهُۥ لَلۡحُسۡنَىٰۚ فَلَنُنَبِّئَنَّ ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُواْ بِمَا عَمِلُواْ وَلَنُذِيقَنَّهُم مِّنۡ عَذَابٍ غَلِيظࣲ‏
41:50.en: And verily, if We cause him to taste mercy after some hurt that hath touched him, he will say: This is my own; and I deem not that the Hour will ever rise, and if I am brought back to my Lord, I surely shall be better off with Him - But We verily shall tell those who disbelieve (all) that they did, and We verily shall make them taste hard punishment

41:51.ar: وَإِذَآ أَنۡعَمۡنَا عَلَى ٱلۡإِنسَٰنِ أَعۡرَضَ وَنَـَٔا بِجَانِبِهِۦ وَإِذَا مَسَّهُ ٱلشَّرُّ فَذُو دُعَآءٍ عَرِيضࣲ‏
41:51.en: When We show favour unto man, he withdraweth and turneth aside, but when ill toucheth him then he aboundeth in prayer

41:52.ar: قُلۡ أَرَءَيۡتُمۡ إِن كَانَ مِنۡ عِندِ ٱللَّهِ ثُمَّ كَفَرۡتُم بِهِۦ مَنۡ أَضَلُّ مِمَّنۡ هُوَ فِي شِقَاقِۭ بَعِيدࣲ‏
41:52.en: Bethink you: If it is from Allah and ye reject it - Who is further astray than one who is at open feud (with Allah)

41:53.ar: سَنُرِيهِمۡ ءَايَٰتِنَا فِي ٱلۡأٓفَاقِ وَفِيٓ أَنفُسِهِمۡ حَتَّىٰ يَتَبَيَّنَ لَهُمۡ أَنَّهُ ٱلۡحَقُّۗ أَوَلَمۡ يَكۡفِ بِرَبِّكَ أَنَّهُۥ عَلَىٰ كُلِّ شَيۡءࣲ شَهِيدٌ
41:53.en: We shall show them Our portents on the horizons and within themselves until it will be manifest unto them that it is the Truth. Doth not thy Lord suffice, since He is Witness over all things

41:54.ar: أَلَآ إِنَّهُمۡ فِي مِرۡيَةࣲ مِّن لِّقَآءِ رَبِّهِمۡۗ أَلَآ إِنَّهُۥ بِكُلِّ شَيۡءࣲ مُّحِيطُۢ
41:54.en: How! Are they still in doubt about the meeting with their Lord? Lo! Is not He surrounding all things

41:33.ar: وَمَنۡ أَحۡسَنُ قَوۡلࣰ ا مِّمَّن دَعَآ إِلَى ٱللَّهِ وَعَمِلَ صَٰلِحࣰ ا وَقَالَ إِنَّنِي مِنَ ٱلۡمُسۡلِمِينَ
41:33.en: And who is better in speech than him who prayeth unto his Lord and doeth right, and saith: Lo! I am of those who are muslims (surrender unto Him)

41:34.ar: وَلَا تَسۡتَوِي ٱلۡحَسَنَةُ وَلَا ٱلسَّيِّئَةُۚ ٱدۡفَعۡ بِٱلَّتِي هِيَ أَحۡسَنُ فَإِذَا ٱلَّذِي بَيۡنَكَ وَبَيۡنَهُۥ عَدَٰوَةࣱ كَأَنَّهُۥ وَلِيٌّ حَمِيمࣱ‏
41:34.en: The good deed and the evil deed are not alike. Repel the evil deed with one which is better, then lo! he, between whom and thee there was enmity (will become) as though he was a bosom friend

41:35.ar: وَمَا يُلَقَّىٰهَآ إِلَّا ٱلَّذِينَ صَبَرُواْ وَمَا يُلَقَّىٰهَآ إِلَّا ذُو حَظٍّ عَظِيمࣲ‏
41:35.en: But none is granted it save those who are steadfast, and none is granted it save the owner of great happiness

41:36.ar: وَإِمَّا يَنزَغَنَّكَ مِنَ ٱلشَّيۡطَٰنِ نَزۡغࣱ فَٱسۡتَعِذۡ بِٱللَّهِۖ إِنَّهُۥ هُوَ ٱلسَّمِيعُ ٱلۡعَلِيمُ
41:36.en: And if a whisper from the devil reach thee (O Muhammad) then seek refuge in Allah. Lo! He is the Hearer, the Knower

70:21.en: And, when good befalleth him, grudging

89:15.ar: فَأَمَّا ٱلۡإِنسَٰنُ إِذَا مَا ٱبۡتَلَىٰهُ رَبُّهُۥ فَأَكۡرَمَهُۥ وَنَعَّمَهُۥ فَيَقُولُ رَبِّيٓ أَكۡرَمَنِ
89:15.en: As for man, whenever his Lord trieth him by honouring him, and is gracious unto him, he saith: My Lord honoureth me

89:16.ar: وَأَمَّآ إِذَا مَا ٱبۡتَلَىٰهُ فَقَدَرَ عَلَيۡهِ رِزۡقَهُۥ فَيَقُولُ رَبِّيٓ أَهَٰنَنِ
89:16.en: But whenever He trieth him by straitening his means of life, he saith: My Lord despiseth me

21:35.ar: كُلُّ نَفۡسࣲ ذَآئِقَةُ ٱلۡمَوۡتِۗ وَنَبۡلُوكُم بِٱلشَّرِّ وَٱلۡخَيۡرِ فِتۡنَةࣰۖ وَإِلَيۡنَا تُرۡجَعُونَ
21:35.en: Every soul must taste of death, and We try you with evil and with good, for ordeal. And unto Us ye will be returned

93:5.en: And verily thy Lord will give unto thee so that thou wilt be content

mNYF8TyuG7A.speaker: adnan
mNYF8TyuG7A.speaker_note: concluding session of the sheikh's Ramadan tafseer of Fussilat; single voice
mNYF8TyuG7A.title: Tafseer of Surat Fussilat: Verses 49-54
mNYF8TyuG7A.one_line: The closing verses of Fussilat portray the untrained soul swinging between despair and arrogance, and end with signs, certainty in meeting Allah, and His encompassing knowledge.
mNYF8TyuG7A.summary: He presents the end of Fussilat as the mirror image of the good-character dawah described in its middle: a portrait of the soul that has never been purified. Verse 49 shows a person who never tires of asking for more, yet despairs at the lightest touch of hardship. Verse 50 has the same person, once relieved, claiming the success as his own, doubting the Hour, and assuming he will be treated well because he is a good person; the sheikh challenges anyone to name the criteria for calling himself good and warns against comforting comparisons with others. He reframes life's highs and lows as tests: the worst day may be the winning ticket on Judgment Day. Graduation and promotions hide how often Allah bailed us out, and a distorted view of reality eventually catches up. The Prophet strove for twenty-three years and passed away before seeing the fruit, mastering patience so well that it looks easy. Verse 51 adds the person who turns away when blessed and makes long dua only when hit again, which is why Ramadan exists to restart the conversation with Allah. The finale asks the rejecter to consider that the Quran might be true, promises signs in the horizons and the self, locates the root problem in doubt about meeting Allah, and closes with Allah encompassing everything, so His guidance can be trusted.

outline.heading: Opening
The closing verses as the opposite of good-character dawah
outline.gist: After verses 33-36 showed character-based dawah, the ending shows what the unpurified soul does when things go well or badly.

outline.heading: Never tired of asking for good
outline.gist: People always want more; compare what you have with what you hope for, especially with the privileges of life in the West.

outline.heading: Only dust fills the son of Adam
outline.gist: The hadith of wanting a second valley of gold: only death, or finding Allah, fills the inner emptiness, and the Prophet himself was fulfilled.

outline.heading: 'Massahu': the lightest touch of hardship
outline.gist: The word means minimal contact, yet even that little evil plunges the person into despair.

outline.heading: Despair at a small portion of bad
outline.gist: Life is a mix of good and bad, yet we expect only good and panic at the slightest difficulty.

outline.heading: A description of a problem, not a model
outline.gist: These verses describe character to avoid and reveal a lack of clarity about what Allah taught.

outline.heading: 'This is mine': taking credit for relief
outline.gist: After hardship lifts, the person boasts of his own effort, drifts toward agnosticism about the Hour, and assumes Allah will treat him well anyway.

outline.heading: Who told you that you are a good person?
outline.gist: Calling others good is a kind assumption, but calling yourself good, or comparing yourself with those who do not pray, is arrogance; only Allah decides.

outline.heading: Top of the hill, bottom of the valley
outline.gist: Highs and lows are illusions; the day you suffered most may be your winning ticket on Judgment Day, and abundance does not mean Allah loves you.

outline.heading: Everything is a test
outline.gist: Plenty tests gratitude and scarcity tests patience; feeling upset for a moment is normal, but how you respond must differ.

outline.heading: Success is Allah's bounty
outline.gist: Millions strive and still fail; those who succeed and claim it as their own often end up treating faith as an optional accessory.

outline.heading: How easily you could have failed
outline.gist: Allah will show each person exactly what they did; graduates should remember how many times Allah bailed them out.

outline.heading: A distorted reality comes back like a boomerang
outline.gist: Seeing yourself accurately brings some remorse but grounds you and makes you humble.

outline.heading: We are entitled to nothing
outline.gist: Praying in the masjid in Ramadan is already among the greatest blessings; ask for more, but expect life to throw curveballs.

outline.heading: The Prophet did not live to see the fruit
outline.gist: After twenty-three years of striving he was taken just before witnessing what his students would carry, so we should look at his life before complaining.

outline.heading: Masters make it look easy
outline.gist: Like a world-class tennis or chess player, the Prophet handled hardship so well that we miss the pain and frustration he hid.

outline.heading: Turning away in plenty, long dua in hardship
outline.gist: The blessed person turns aside with nose held high, and when hit again makes broad dua; life starts and ends with asking.

outline.heading: These patterns ruin dawah through behaviour
outline.gist: If we fall into any of these patterns, whatever advice we give others will mean little.

outline.heading: Ramadan restarts the conversation with Allah
outline.gist: We ask, receive and walk away for a year; Allah sometimes takes back a blessing so we return, and sacred seasons bring us back to Him.

outline.heading: The servant whose dua is delayed
outline.gist: Allah may delay answering a pious servant because He loves to hear him ask and knows he would stop once he received it.

outline.heading: What if it is from Allah?
outline.gist: Muslims follow evidence and listen objectively; the verse asks rejecters to at least consider that the Quran may be true.

outline.heading: Torn far away: judging what you never heard
outline.gist: Shiqaq is a rift from reason; refusing to study what is presented leaves you lost, unable to form a fair judgment.

outline.heading: Signs in the horizons and in the self
outline.gist: Allah promises signs until the truth is clear; the verse is about the human inner life, not a scientific argument.

outline.heading: Why are we miserable when our needs are met?
outline.gist: Safety, food and freedom satisfy every other creature, but humans remain unhappy because a spiritual part of them is neglected.

outline.heading: Is it not enough that your Lord witnesses all?
outline.gist: Allah is ash-Shaheed, present for every moment you lived even when no one else saw.

outline.heading: The root problem: doubt about meeting Allah
outline.gist: You will certainly meet the One who brought you here; without that certainty this world is all you have, so hardship crushes you and success breeds vanity.

outline.heading: He encompasses everything: trust His full picture
outline.gist: We see only the detail we are stuck in, whether struggle or promotion; Allah sees the whole, so His guidance is what we need.

outline.heading: Outro

themes.label: Tazkiyah: purifying and training the self
themes.note: The verses diagnose the untrained soul that despairs in hardship and grows vain in ease.

themes.label: Humility vs vanity and arrogance
themes.note: Claiming success as one's own and calling oneself a good person are arrogance; success is Allah's bounty.

themes.label: Trials, hardship and resilience
themes.note: Highs and lows are tests, and the Prophet's life shows hardship handled with mastery.

themes.label: The Prophet's attributes, character and example
themes.note: He strove for twenty-three years without seeing the fruit and hid his pain so well it looks easy.

themes.label: Dua and invocation
themes.note: People make dua only when in need; Ramadan and delayed answers keep the conversation with Allah going.

themes.label: Dawah, outreach and representing Islam
themes.note: Bad character undoes dawah, and the Quran asks listeners to give it a fair hearing.

themes.label: Mental health, anxiety and emotional wellbeing
themes.note: Unhappiness despite met needs points to a neglected spiritual dimension.

themes.label: Eman: faith, certainty, doubt
themes.note: Doubt about meeting Allah is the root of the behaviours described, and His encompassing knowledge grounds trust.

quran.point: The middle of the surah describes dawah through good character, which the ending mirrors.
Humans panic in hardship and withhold in ease, except those who pray.
Thinking abundance means Allah honours you and scarcity means He humiliates you.
Good and bad are both tests.
The Prophet will be fully satisfied in the Hereafter.

hadith.gist: If the son of Adam had a valley of gold he would want a second; nothing fills him but dust.
Allah delays answering a servant's dua because He loves to hear him ask.

maxims: Your worst day may be your winning ticket
Who gave you the criteria to call yourself good?
Masters make it look easy
There is no up and down, only tests

stories.point: He passed away before seeing the fruit of his striving, so we should not complain about unrewarded effort.

stories.who: A pious servant whose dua is delayed
stories.point: Delay can be Allah keeping a servant close because the servant would stop asking once answered.

contemporary: Success podcasts and self-help blogs that credit personal recipes for achievement
takeaways: When hardship touches you, accept the moment of upset but do not slide into despair.
Attribute success to Allah and remember how often He bailed you out.
Stop calling yourself a good person or comparing yourself with others.
Keep talking to Allah after Ramadan, not only when you need something.
Give the Quran a real hearing and build certainty that you will meet Allah.

42:38.ar: وَٱلَّذِينَ ٱسۡتَجَابُواْ لِرَبِّهِمۡ وَأَقَامُواْ ٱلصَّلَوٰةَ وَأَمۡرُهُمۡ شُورَىٰ بَيۡنَهُمۡ وَمِمَّا رَزَقۡنَٰهُمۡ يُنفِقُونَ
42:38.en: And those who answer the call of their Lord and establish worship, and whose affairs are a matter of counsel, and who spend of what We have bestowed on them

43:31.ar: وَقَالُواْ لَوۡلَا نُزِّلَ هَٰذَا ٱلۡقُرۡءَانُ عَلَىٰ رَجُلࣲ مِّنَ ٱلۡقَرۡيَتَيۡنِ عَظِيمٍ
43:31.en: And they say: If only this Qur'an had been revealed to some great man of the two towns

43:32.ar: أَهُمۡ يَقۡسِمُونَ رَحۡمَتَ رَبِّكَۚ نَحۡنُ قَسَمۡنَا بَيۡنَهُم مَّعِيشَتَهُمۡ فِي ٱلۡحَيَوٰةِ ٱلدُّنۡيَاۚ وَرَفَعۡنَا بَعۡضَهُمۡ فَوۡقَ بَعۡضࣲ دَرَجَٰتࣲ لِّيَتَّخِذَ بَعۡضُهُم بَعۡضࣰ ا سُخۡرِيࣰّ اۗ وَرَحۡمَتُ رَبِّكَ خَيۡرࣱ مِّمَّا يَجۡمَعُونَ
43:32.en: Is it they who apportion thy Lord's mercy? We have apportioned among them their livelihood in the life of the world, and raised some of them above others in rank that some of them may take labour from others; and the mercy of thy Lord is better than (the wealth) that they amass

43:33.ar: وَلَوۡلَآ أَن يَكُونَ ٱلنَّاسُ أُمَّةࣰ وَٰحِدَةࣰ لَّجَعَلۡنَا لِمَن يَكۡفُرُ بِٱلرَّحۡمَٰنِ لِبُيُوتِهِمۡ سُقُفࣰ ا مِّن فِضَّةࣲ وَمَعَارِجَ عَلَيۡهَا يَظۡهَرُونَ
43:33.en: And were it not that mankind would have become one community, We might well have appointed, for those who disbelieve in the Beneficent, roofs of silver for their houses and stairs (of silver) whereby to mount

43:34.ar: وَلِبُيُوتِهِمۡ أَبۡوَٰبࣰ ا وَسُرُرًا عَلَيۡهَا يَتَّكِـُٔونَ
43:34.en: And for their houses doors (of silver) and couches of silver whereon to recline

43:35.ar: وَزُخۡرُفࣰ اۚ وَإِن كُلُّ ذَٰلِكَ لَمَّا مَتَٰعُ ٱلۡحَيَوٰةِ ٱلدُّنۡيَاۚ وَٱلۡأٓخِرَةُ عِندَ رَبِّكَ لِلۡمُتَّقِينَ
43:35.en: And ornaments of gold. Yet all that would have been but a provision of the life of the world. And the Hereafter with your Lord would have been for those who keep from evil

43:51.ar: وَنَادَىٰ فِرۡعَوۡنُ فِي قَوۡمِهِۦ قَالَ يَٰقَوۡمِ أَلَيۡسَ لِي مُلۡكُ مِصۡرَ وَهَٰذِهِ ٱلۡأَنۡهَٰرُ تَجۡرِي مِن تَحۡتِيٓۚ أَفَلَا تُبۡصِرُونَ
43:51.en: And Pharaoh caused a proclamation to be made among his people saying: O my people! Is not mine the sovereignty of Egypt and these rivers flowing under me? Can ye not then discern

43:52.ar: أَمۡ أَنَا۠ خَيۡرࣱ مِّنۡ هَٰذَا ٱلَّذِي هُوَ مَهِينࣱ وَلَا يَكَادُ يُبِينُ
43:52.en: I am surely better than this fellow, who is despicable and can hardly make (his meaning) plain

43:53.ar: فَلَوۡلَآ أُلۡقِيَ عَلَيۡهِ أَسۡوِرَةࣱ مِّن ذَهَبٍ أَوۡ جَآءَ مَعَهُ ٱلۡمَلَٰٓئِكَةُ مُقۡتَرِنِينَ
43:53.en: Why, then, have armlets of gold not been set upon him, or angels sent along with him

43:54.ar: فَٱسۡتَخَفَّ قَوۡمَهُۥ فَأَطَاعُوهُۚ إِنَّهُمۡ كَانُواْ قَوۡمࣰ ا فَٰسِقِينَ
43:54.en: Thus he persuaded his people to make light (of Moses), and they obeyed him. Lo! they were a wanton folk

43:55.ar: فَلَمَّآ ءَاسَفُونَا ٱنتَقَمۡنَا مِنۡهُمۡ فَأَغۡرَقۡنَٰهُمۡ أَجۡمَعِينَ
43:55.en: So, when they angered Us, We punished them and drowned them every one

43:56.ar: فَجَعَلۡنَٰهُمۡ سَلَفࣰ ا وَمَثَلࣰ ا لِّلۡأٓخِرِينَ
43:56.en: And We made them a thing past, and an example for those after (them)

44:25.en: How many were the gardens and the watersprings that they left behind

44:26.en: And the cornlands and the goodly sites

44:27.en: And pleasant things wherein they took delight

44:28.en: Even so (it was), and We made it an inheritance for other folk

44:29.ar: فَمَا بَكَتۡ عَلَيۡهِمُ ٱلسَّمَآءُ وَٱلۡأَرۡضُ وَمَا كَانُواْ مُنظَرِينَ
44:29.en: And the heaven and the earth wept not for them, nor were they reprieved

45:14.ar: قُل لِّلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُواْ يَغۡفِرُواْ لِلَّذِينَ لَا يَرۡجُونَ أَيَّامَ ٱللَّهِ لِيَجۡزِيَ قَوۡمَۢا بِمَا كَانُواْ يَكۡسِبُونَ
45:14.en: Tell those who believe to forgive those who hope not for the days of Allah; in order that He may requite folk what they used to earn

46:15.ar: وَوَصَّيۡنَا ٱلۡإِنسَٰنَ بِوَٰلِدَيۡهِ إِحۡسَٰنًاۖ حَمَلَتۡهُ أُمُّهُۥ كُرۡهࣰ ا وَوَضَعَتۡهُ كُرۡهࣰ اۖ وَحَمۡلُهُۥ وَفِصَٰلُهُۥ ثَلَٰثُونَ شَهۡرًاۚ حَتَّىٰٓ إِذَا بَلَغَ أَشُدَّهُۥ وَبَلَغَ أَرۡبَعِينَ سَنَةࣰ قَالَ رَبِّ أَوۡزِعۡنِيٓ أَنۡ أَشۡكُرَ نِعۡمَتَكَ ٱلَّتِيٓ أَنۡعَمۡتَ عَلَيَّ وَعَلَىٰ وَٰلِدَيَّ وَأَنۡ أَعۡمَلَ صَٰلِحࣰ ا تَرۡضَىٰهُ وَأَصۡلِحۡ لِي فِي ذُرِّيَّتِيٓۖ إِنِّي تُبۡتُ إِلَيۡكَ وَإِنِّي مِنَ ٱلۡمُسۡلِمِينَ
46:15.en: And We have commended unto man kindness toward parents. His mother beareth him with reluctance, and bringeth him forth with reluctance, and the bearing of him and the weaning of him is thirty months, till, when he attaineth full strength and reacheth forty years, he saith: My Lord! Arouse me that I may give thanks for the favour wherewith Thou hast favoured me and my parents, and that I may do right acceptable unto Thee. And be gracious unto me in the matter of my seed. Lo! I have turned unto Thee repentant, and lo! I am of those who surrender (unto Thee)

46:16.ar: أُوْلَٰٓئِكَ ٱلَّذِينَ نَتَقَبَّلُ عَنۡهُمۡ أَحۡسَنَ مَا عَمِلُواْ وَنَتَجَاوَزُ عَن سَيِّـَٔاتِهِمۡ فِيٓ أَصۡحَٰبِ ٱلۡجَنَّةِۖ وَعۡدَ ٱلصِّدۡقِ ٱلَّذِي كَانُواْ يُوعَدُونَ
46:16.en: Those are they from whom We accept the best of what they do, and overlook their evil deeds. (They are) among the owners of the Garden. This is the true promise which they were promised (in the world)

46:17.ar: وَٱلَّذِي قَالَ لِوَٰلِدَيۡهِ أُفࣲّ لَّكُمَآ أَتَعِدَانِنِيٓ أَنۡ أُخۡرَجَ وَقَدۡ خَلَتِ ٱلۡقُرُونُ مِن قَبۡلِي وَهُمَا يَسۡتَغِيثَانِ ٱللَّهَ وَيۡلَكَ ءَامِنۡ إِنَّ وَعۡدَ ٱللَّهِ حَقࣱّ فَيَقُولُ مَا هَٰذَآ إِلَّآ أَسَٰطِيرُ ٱلۡأَوَّلِينَ
46:17.en: And whoso saith unto his parents: Fie upon you both! Do ye threaten me that I shall be brought forth (again) when generations before me have passed away? And they twain cry unto Allah for help (and say): Woe unto thee! Believe! Lo! the promise of Allah is true. But he saith: This is naught save fables of the men of old

46:29.ar: وَإِذۡ صَرَفۡنَآ إِلَيۡكَ نَفَرࣰ ا مِّنَ ٱلۡجِنِّ يَسۡتَمِعُونَ ٱلۡقُرۡءَانَ فَلَمَّا حَضَرُوهُ قَالُوٓاْ أَنصِتُواْۖ فَلَمَّا قُضِيَ وَلَّوۡاْ إِلَىٰ قَوۡمِهِم مُّنذِرِينَ
46:29.en: And when We inclined toward thee (Muhammad) certain of the jinn, who wished to hear the Qur'an and, when they were in its presence, said: Give ear! and, when it was finished, turned back to their people, warning

46:30.ar: قَالُواْ يَٰقَوۡمَنَآ إِنَّا سَمِعۡنَا كِتَٰبًا أُنزِلَ مِنۢ بَعۡدِ مُوسَىٰ مُصَدِّقࣰ ا لِّمَا بَيۡنَ يَدَيۡهِ يَهۡدِيٓ إِلَى ٱلۡحَقِّ وَإِلَىٰ طَرِيقࣲ مُّسۡتَقِيمࣲ‏
46:30.en: They said: O our people! Lo! we have heard a scripture which hath been revealed after Moses, confirming that which was before it, guiding unto the truth and a right road

46:31.ar: يَٰقَوۡمَنَآ أَجِيبُواْ دَاعِيَ ٱللَّهِ وَءَامِنُواْ بِهِۦ يَغۡفِرۡ لَكُم مِّن ذُنُوبِكُمۡ وَيُجِرۡكُم مِّنۡ عَذَابٍ أَلِيمࣲ‏
46:31.en: O our people! respond to Allah's summoner and believe in Him. He will forgive you some of your sins and guard you from a painful doom

46:32.ar: وَمَن لَّا يُجِبۡ دَاعِيَ ٱللَّهِ فَلَيۡسَ بِمُعۡجِزࣲ فِي ٱلۡأَرۡضِ وَلَيۡسَ لَهُۥ مِن دُونِهِۦٓ أَوۡلِيَآءُۚ أُوْلَٰٓئِكَ فِي ضَلَٰلࣲ مُّبِينٍ
46:32.en: And whoso respondeth not to Allah's summoner he can nowise escape in the earth, and he hath no protecting friends instead of Him. Such are in error manifest

46:35.ar: فَٱصۡبِرۡ كَمَا صَبَرَ أُوْلُواْ ٱلۡعَزۡمِ مِنَ ٱلرُّسُلِ وَلَا تَسۡتَعۡجِل لَّهُمۡۚ كَأَنَّهُمۡ يَوۡمَ يَرَوۡنَ مَا يُوعَدُونَ لَمۡ يَلۡبَثُوٓاْ إِلَّا سَاعَةࣰ مِّن نَّهَارِۭۚ بَلَٰغࣱۚ فَهَلۡ يُهۡلَكُ إِلَّا ٱلۡقَوۡمُ ٱلۡفَٰسِقُونَ
46:35.en: Then have patience (O Muhammad) even as the stout of heart among the messengers (of old) had patience, and seek not to hasten on (the doom) for them. On the day when they see that which they are promised (it will seem to them) as though they had tarried but an hour of daylight. A clear message. Shall any be destroyed save evil-living folk

3:159.ar: فَبِمَا رَحۡمَةࣲ مِّنَ ٱللَّهِ لِنتَ لَهُمۡۖ وَلَوۡ كُنتَ فَظًّا غَلِيظَ ٱلۡقَلۡبِ لَٱنفَضُّواْ مِنۡ حَوۡلِكَۖ فَٱعۡفُ عَنۡهُمۡ وَٱسۡتَغۡفِرۡ لَهُمۡ وَشَاوِرۡهُمۡ فِي ٱلۡأَمۡرِۖ فَإِذَا عَزَمۡتَ فَتَوَكَّلۡ عَلَى ٱللَّهِۚ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ يُحِبُّ ٱلۡمُتَوَكِّلِينَ
3:159.en: It was by the mercy of Allah that thou wast lenient with them (O Muhammad), for if thou hadst been stern and fierce of heart they would have dispersed from round about thee. So pardon them and ask forgiveness for them and consult with them upon the conduct of affairs. And when thou art resolved, then put thy trust in Allah. Lo! Allah loveth those who put their trust (in Him)

sCuuR9mU99M.speaker: adnan
sCuuR9mU99M.speaker_note: leads the nightly reflections, says he has taught the tafsir of these surahs three times in London and speaks of the city's community
sCuuR9mU99M.title: Ramadan 2023, Night 24: Quranic Reflections (Al-Shura to Al-Ahqaf)
sCuuR9mU99M.one_line: The Ha-Mim surahs on dawah: shura and community unity, the materialist measure of greatness, the delusion of ownership, forgiving the heedless, and leaving outcomes to Allah.
sCuuR9mU99M.summary: He recaps the Ha-Mim cluster: what helps dawah, what harms it, and the reminder that outcomes are Allah's, which is no excuse to blame the audience instead of fixing the delivery. Most of the night goes to shura in 42:38. Consultation is a decision-making system; without one, Muslim neighbours celebrate Eid on different days and masajid splinter by ethnicity, as in other cities. The Prophet followed the majority at Uhud against his own view and kept consulting even after the losses, so the problem today is big egos. He values unity over method on matters of practice, and says a bad leader is better than none. In al-Zukhruf, Quraysh and Pharaoh judge prophets by wealth, power and fluency, a materialist measure and an ad hominem trick; masajid run like businesses fall into it. Al-Dukhan's gardens left behind expose the delusion of ownership: we are entitled to nothing and hold everything, even the planet, in trust, like a traveller resting under a tree. Al-Jathiyah tells believers to forgive those heedless of Allah rather than look down on them, as a bleeding prophet prayed for his people. Al-Ahqaf closes: be patient, show up daily, and let Allah decide who responds.

outline.heading: Recap: what helps and what harms dawah
outline.gist: Take it to the right people with a living connection to Allah, through character and organization; materialism, delusional thinking and arrogance ruin it.

outline.heading: Al-Ahqaf: you cannot control who responds
outline.gist: Knowing outcomes are Allah's removes the stress of trying to force people.

outline.heading: Fix the delivery, do not blame the audience
outline.gist: A business that fails does not blame customers; if dawah does not land, the product is fine and the delivery needs work.

outline.heading: A cluster for Muslim minorities in the West
outline.gist: He has taught these surahs three times in London because their meanings shape how Muslims living as minorities approach things.

outline.heading: The believers who can carry dawah
outline.gist: Allah lists their attributes, and in the middle is the word that names the surah.

outline.heading: Consultation on matters affecting everyone
outline.gist: The Prophet was commanded to consult on communal decisions, not on revelation.

outline.heading: Shura is a decision-making system
outline.gist: Believers pray, rely on Allah and give zakah, but they also organize how they decide, down to when Eid will be.

outline.heading: Two Eids in one neighbourhood
outline.gist: Neighbours in semi-detached homes celebrating on different days is a failure of organization, not of faith.

outline.heading: Everyone involved, through representatives
outline.gist: Joint decisions are needed on Ramadan, communal wealth, youth programming, outreach to wider Canadian society and political involvement.

outline.heading: Structure or everyone does what they want
outline.gist: Without a hierarchy for decisions nothing gets done; he would move to a city where Muslims are organized.

outline.heading: Unity over method
outline.gist: Calculation or sighting does not matter to him as long as a city's Muslims act together.

outline.heading: The Prophet followed the majority at Uhud
outline.gist: He wanted to defend from inside Madinah but went out because most wanted to; the command to consult had come years earlier.

outline.heading: After Uhud: just listen to the elders
outline.gist: Having lost Hamzah and others, some elders argued he should stop consulting people.

outline.heading: Consultation was not optional; egos are the obstacle
outline.gist: He kept consulting to the end of his life; what blocks shura today is big egos and personal agendas.

outline.heading: When every masjid is its own country
outline.gist: London risks becoming like cities in the GTA and the US where each masjid goes its own way on everything.

outline.heading: Swallow your ego: a bad leader beats none
outline.gist: Islam is about unity; within a few years of disorder masajid split by ethnicity and arrival date.

outline.heading: Practices are designed for disagreement
outline.gist: The spirit is unity; on simple matters of practice differing opinions are expected, so let them go and stick together.

outline.heading: Creed is not up for consultation
outline.gist: Fundamental values are settled; consultation covers practical arrangements, community direction and outreach, as at Uhud.

outline.heading: Do not add to the ummah's weakness
outline.gist: We are weak already; pay the small price of staying quiet for the greater goal of unity.

outline.heading: Why not a great man of the two cities?
outline.gist: Quraysh objected that the Quran should have come to a man of wealth and status, the materialist mindset that ruins dawah.

outline.heading: The Prophet was a minimalist by choice
outline.gist: He could have earned wealth but gave away what he had, more visibly after prophethood.

outline.heading: Do they distribute your Lord's mercy?
outline.gist: Judging status by wealth or power is wrong, and Allah alone decides who receives His mercy.

outline.heading: We divided their livelihood so they need one another
outline.gist: A doctor needs a mechanic and a teacher needs a plumber; no one is greater for money, degrees or followers.

outline.heading: Your Lord's mercy is better than what they gather
outline.gist: Allah is the one who gave the wealth they use to rank people.

outline.heading: Zukhruf: shiny but worthless
outline.gist: If people would not all abandon faith, Allah would give disbelievers every ornament, because it is short-lived and worth nothing.

outline.heading: A materialist matrix for judging greatness
outline.gist: Judging who is great by wealth alone is the thread running through this passage.

outline.heading: Masajid run like businesses
outline.gist: When a newcomer is seen as a dollar sign and people's worth is measured by wealth rather than closeness to Allah, dawah stops working.

outline.heading: Interlude
Pharaoh: is not Egypt mine?
outline.gist: He boasts of the kingdom and rivers at his feet and mocks Musa as weak, without an army, and unable to speak clearly.

outline.heading: He made fools of his people, then drowned
outline.gist: His people followed him; the man with rivers under his feet ended with the sea over his head.

outline.heading: Attacking the person, not the point
outline.gist: Pharaoh's argument is the ad hominem fallacy, a trick to stop people hearing the argument; this framing of the story appears only in al-Zukhruf.

outline.heading: How many gardens they left behind
outline.gist: Al-Dukhan's lesson on delusional thinking: Pharaoh's people left everything they enjoyed to others.

outline.heading: The delusion that we own anything
outline.gist: Looking at our house, car and bank account, it is hard to imagine they will go to someone who soon forgets us.

outline.heading: Held in trust, like the planet
outline.gist: What we have is a gift to use briefly and return as we found it, just as the earth should be handed back healthy.

outline.heading: You are entitled to nothing
outline.gist: Be honest: how much of who you are did you build yourself, and how much came from others?

outline.heading: A traveller resting under a tree
outline.gist: The land we stand on belonged to others who felt the same; the Prophet likened this life to a rider pausing in the shade.

outline.heading: Take only a traveller's provision
outline.gist: Take from the world what gets you to your destination; delusions of ownership ruin behaviour, mentality and dawah.

outline.heading: Neither heaven nor earth wept for them
outline.gist: When we die the world goes on and our wealth is divided by Allah's rules; it was never ours.

outline.heading: Al-Jathiyah: arrogance as a barrier
outline.gist: The surah warns that arrogance blocks dawah.

outline.heading: Tell the believers to forgive the heedless
outline.gist: Those who understand reality forgive people who have no hope in the days of Allah: His creation, blessings and the Day of accounting.

outline.heading: No condescension: they do not know
outline.gist: Do not judge, look down on or hold others to your standards; they have no idea what they will regret.

outline.heading: A prophet wiping blood from his face
outline.gist: The Prophet told of a prophet beaten bloody who prayed for his people because they did not know; a true movement is never arrogant.

outline.heading: The truly guided never look down
outline.gist: Allah will give everyone their due; the believer's part is to forgive, not hate.

outline.heading: Be patient like the resolute messengers
outline.gist: Do not rush people; al-Ahqaf reminds you that you cannot control the outcome.

outline.heading: Two sons of pious parents
outline.gist: One son believes and the other mocks resurrection; parents cannot control which way a child goes.

outline.heading: The jinn who heard him by chance
outline.gist: After years of his people refusing, jinn who overheard his prayer believed and carried the message to others with no effort from him.

outline.heading: Just show up every day
outline.gist: The least expected people respond; use the right tools, avoid the harmful ones, and keep going.

outline.heading: Do not hasten for them
outline.gist: Let people decide in their own time; on the Day they will feel they lived only an hour.

outline.heading: Outro

51:56.ar: وَمَا خَلَقۡتُ ٱلۡجِنَّ وَٱلۡإِنسَ إِلَّا لِيَعۡبُدُونِ
51:56.en: I created the jinn and humankind only that they might worship Me

2:30.ar: وَإِذۡ قَالَ رَبُّكَ لِلۡمَلَٰٓئِكَةِ إِنِّي جَاعِلࣱ فِي ٱلۡأَرۡضِ خَلِيفَةࣰۖ قَالُوٓاْ أَتَجۡعَلُ فِيهَا مَن يُفۡسِدُ فِيهَا وَيَسۡفِكُ ٱلدِّمَآءَ وَنَحۡنُ نُسَبِّحُ بِحَمۡدِكَ وَنُقَدِّسُ لَكَۖ قَالَ إِنِّيٓ أَعۡلَمُ مَا لَا تَعۡلَمُونَ
2:30.en: And when thy Lord said unto the angels: Lo! I am about to place a viceroy in the earth, they said: Wilt thou place therein one who will do harm therein and will shed blood, while we, we hymn Thy praise and sanctify Thee? He said: Surely I know that which ye know not

40:60.ar: وَقَالَ رَبُّكُمُ ٱدۡعُونِيٓ أَسۡتَجِبۡ لَكُمۡۚ إِنَّ ٱلَّذِينَ يَسۡتَكۡبِرُونَ عَنۡ عِبَادَتِي سَيَدۡخُلُونَ جَهَنَّمَ دَاخِرِينَ
40:60.en: And your Lord hath said: Pray unto Me and I will hear your prayer. Lo! those who scorn My service, they will enter hell, disgraced

2:195.ar: وَأَنفِقُواْ فِي سَبِيلِ ٱللَّهِ وَلَا تُلۡقُواْ بِأَيۡدِيكُمۡ إِلَى ٱلتَّهۡلُكَةِ وَأَحۡسِنُوٓاْۚ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ يُحِبُّ ٱلۡمُحۡسِنِينَ
2:195.en: Spend your wealth for the cause of Allah, and be not cast by your own hands to ruin; and do good. Lo! Allah loveth the beneficent

2:216.ar: كُتِبَ عَلَيۡكُمُ ٱلۡقِتَالُ وَهُوَ كُرۡهࣱ لَّكُمۡۖ وَعَسَىٰٓ أَن تَكۡرَهُواْ شَيۡـࣰٔ ا وَهُوَ خَيۡرࣱ لَّكُمۡۖ وَعَسَىٰٓ أَن تُحِبُّواْ شَيۡـࣰٔ ا وَهُوَ شَرࣱّ لَّكُمۡۚ وَٱللَّهُ يَعۡلَمُ وَأَنتُمۡ لَا تَعۡلَمُونَ
2:216.en: Warfare is ordained for you, though it is hateful unto you; but it may happen that ye hate a thing which is good for you, and it may happen that ye love a thing which is bad for you. Allah knoweth, ye know not

35:8.ar: أَفَمَن زُيِّنَ لَهُۥ سُوٓءُ عَمَلِهِۦ فَرَءَاهُ حَسَنࣰ اۖ فَإِنَّ ٱللَّهَ يُضِلُّ مَن يَشَآءُ وَيَهۡدِي مَن يَشَآءُۖ فَلَا تَذۡهَبۡ نَفۡسُكَ عَلَيۡهِمۡ حَسَرَٰتٍۚ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ عَلِيمُۢ بِمَا يَصۡنَعُونَ
35:8.en: Is he, the evil of whose deeds is made fairseeming unto him so that he deemeth it good, (other than Satan's dupe)? Allah verily sendeth whom He will astray, and guideth whom He will; so let not thy soul expire in sighings for them. Lo! Allah is Aware of what they do

76:30.ar: وَمَا تَشَآءُونَ إِلَّآ أَن يَشَآءَ ٱللَّهُۚ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ كَانَ عَلِيمًا حَكِيمࣰ ا
76:30.en: Yet ye will not, unless Allah willeth. Lo! Allah is Knower, Wise

78:23.en: They will abide therein for ages

2:111.ar: وَقَالُواْ لَن يَدۡخُلَ ٱلۡجَنَّةَ إِلَّا مَن كَانَ هُودًا أَوۡ نَصَٰرَىٰۗ تِلۡكَ أَمَانِيُّهُمۡۗ قُلۡ هَاتُواْ بُرۡهَٰنَكُمۡ إِن كُنتُمۡ صَٰدِقِينَ
2:111.en: And they say: None entereth paradise unless he be a Jew or a Christian. These are their own desires. Say: Bring your proof (of what ye state) if ye are truthful

2:62.ar: إِنَّ ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُواْ وَٱلَّذِينَ هَادُواْ وَٱلنَّصَٰرَىٰ وَٱلصَّٰبِـِٔينَ مَنۡ ءَامَنَ بِٱللَّهِ وَٱلۡيَوۡمِ ٱلۡأٓخِرِ وَعَمِلَ صَٰلِحࣰ ا فَلَهُمۡ أَجۡرُهُمۡ عِندَ رَبِّهِمۡ وَلَا خَوۡفٌ عَلَيۡهِمۡ وَلَا هُمۡ يَحۡزَنُونَ
2:62.en: Lo! Those who believe (in that which is revealed unto thee, Muhammad), and those who are Jews, and Christians, and Sabaeans - whoever believeth in Allah and the Last Day and doeth right - surely their reward is with their Lord, and there shall no fear come upon them neither shall they grieve

RKAq9JKC78I.speaker: adnan
RKAq9JKC78I.speaker_note: continues his Facing Disbelief series, referring to earlier sessions and his teachers
RKAq9JKC78I.title: Facing Disbelief 6: Evil, Destiny, Dua, Free Will and Punishment
RKAq9JKC78I.one_line: Why Allah created us, how dua really works, free will and divine knowledge, the balance of reward and punishment, and what we control in destiny.
RKAq9JKC78I.summary: He continues the problem of evil by asking why Allah created us at all. We cannot project human motives onto Allah; He told us we are His servants and stewards, and our service to Him reaches Him through serving people. Life itself is the ultimate blessing, and almost everyone wants to live. He then corrects what he calls the Aladdin lamp syndrome: dua is a conversation with Allah, answered in many forms, bound by conditions of humility, possibility and taking the means, and faith must never rest on one granted request since we do not know what is best for us. On free will, he argues that determinism has no support and that our own experience proves a margin of freedom, which Allah will judge individually according to the hand each person was dealt. Allah's knowledge of the future does not compel us, because knowledge does not cause events and He is outside time. Guidance is an easing of the path, not force. Punishment balances an immense reward, scholars have differed on whether Hell is eternal, and Muslims have no right to assign people to Paradise or Hell. Finally he separates what is decreed for us from what we bring on ourselves, and asks people to label events good or bad by how they respond.

outline.heading: Why He created us: no projecting human motives
outline.gist: The only acceptable reason for creation is the one Allah gave; judging Him by what we would do is invalid.

outline.heading: Worship reaches Him through serving people
outline.gist: Allah needs nothing; our service is for us and takes form in stewardship and serving others.

outline.heading: Why would He not create? Life as the ultimate blessing
outline.gist: We cannot grasp non-existence; consciousness, relationships and joy make life the greatest gift despite its pain.

outline.heading: The desire to live and 'I didn't ask to be created'
outline.gist: All life wants to live, and the complaint about not being asked makes no sense since asking requires existing.

outline.heading: Given the tools, you answer for how you use them
outline.gist: Going from nothing to something is beyond our grasp; with the tools and role models given, we are accountable, while those never reached are not.

outline.heading: The Aladdin lamp syndrome
outline.gist: Treating dua as a wish granted on demand is a modern misconception born of centuries of ignorance and colonization.

outline.heading: Dua is a conversation that always gets a response
outline.gist: Allah promised a response, not the exact request: now, later, something better, a harm removed, or reward on Judgment Day.

outline.heading: Conditions of a dua
outline.gist: Ask with humility, for what is possible, after taking the means; a single man asking for a son or a lifelong smoker asking for a cure is unreasonable.

outline.heading: Dua reveals your hopes and plans
outline.gist: Even asking for what is already decreed is fine, since Allah looks at what you ask for and why; dua for haram is rejected outright.

outline.heading: Do not build iman on an answered dua
outline.gist: Many faith crises come from faith built on a granted request; iman rests on the four sources and Islam's coherent picture of God and law.

outline.heading: Missing the answer when it comes through people
outline.gist: Responses often arrive later through ordinary means and go unnoticed unless we look back over our lives.

outline.heading: You do not know what is best for you
outline.gist: What we want and what benefits us differ; an unanswered request may have spared us harm.

outline.heading: Make dua with certainty and accept the answer
outline.gist: Keep asking, never give up, and accept whatever response Allah gives.

outline.heading: Free will versus determinism
outline.gist: Behaviorism and genetic determinism claim we are programmed, an idea that has gained ground recently.

outline.heading: Freedom of choice points to a Creator
outline.gist: Denying God requires denying free will, since a free being in a dead universe must have been placed here.

outline.heading: Aliens and the multiverse are not serious arguments
outline.gist: Other life does not affect faith, and alien-origin theories change nothing about the need for a first cause.

outline.heading: The hand we are dealt
outline.gist: Parents, birthplace and much else are outside our control, and modern comfort delays maturity, so context matters when drawing lessons from the past.

outline.heading: A sacred margin of freedom
outline.gist: Our own experience proves we choose; Islam speaks of a margin of freedom no one may take, and tyrants who do so are those Hell was made for.

outline.heading: Life is Risk, not Snakes and Ladders
outline.gist: We roll dice we did not choose but make real decisions with them, so each person is judged alone.

outline.heading: Two exams of different difficulty
outline.gist: A fair examiner grades a harder paper more gently; worry about your own judgment, not others'.

outline.heading: Allah's knowledge does not compel us
outline.gist: We know the future only by programming things, so we wrongly assume His knowledge removes choice; knowing does not cause an outcome.

outline.heading: Allah is outside time
outline.gist: He sees past, present and future alike, so for Him your life is already lived without being forced.

outline.heading: A God who did not know the future would not be God
outline.gist: Anyone who can be surprised can be beaten and is not worth worshipping.

outline.heading: Seeing every possible choice
outline.gist: Like the multiverse picture, Allah sees every option and simply knows which one you pick.

outline.heading: He guides whom He wills
outline.gist: He chooses based on people's character and choices, and guidance means easing the path and opening the heart, never force.

outline.heading: You will only will if Allah wills
outline.gist: The verse means Allah willed that we have a will, a choice He can take back, not that we lack one.

outline.heading: Why punishment exists
outline.gist: People living under war or tyranny do not ask this; an immense reward needs an equal punishment for justice and real choice.

outline.heading: Without punishment there is no pull toward faith
outline.gist: Paradise is not compelling without its opposite.

outline.heading: Scholars differ on whether Hell is eternal
outline.gist: A difference going back to the companions, based on wording that describes Hell differently from Paradise.

outline.heading: No one owns Paradise
outline.gist: The Quran rejects each group's claim that only they enter; dawah remains a duty, but judging others' end is not ours.

outline.heading: Many categories on the Day of Judgment
outline.gist: In this world we see only believer and disbeliever; on that day Allah judges people by their experiences, so declaring whole nations doomed is arrogant.

outline.heading: If you care, go save them: the dying boy
outline.gist: The Prophet left the boy's deathbed in tears of joy that he was saved; concern for others should drive dawah, not judgment.

outline.heading: You help others to save yourself
outline.gist: Teaching and helping is for your own sake, so no one owes you anything.

outline.heading: What is decreed and what we bring on ourselves
outline.gist: Skin colour, birth and lifespan are given; a careful driver hit by someone is decree, a speeding texter has destined himself.

outline.heading: Unnatural consequences and good and bad as labels
outline.gist: Undeserved failure calls for patience, undeserved success for gratitude or alarm, as continued blessing amid sin is a warning; you label events good or bad by your response.

outline.heading: Outro

4:46.ar: مِّنَ ٱلَّذِينَ هَادُواْ يُحَرِّفُونَ ٱلۡكَلِمَ عَن مَّوَاضِعِهِۦ وَيَقُولُونَ سَمِعۡنَا وَعَصَيۡنَا وَٱسۡمَعۡ غَيۡرَ مُسۡمَعࣲ وَرَٰعِنَا لَيَّۢا بِأَلۡسِنَتِهِمۡ وَطَعۡنࣰ ا فِي ٱلدِّينِۚ وَلَوۡ أَنَّهُمۡ قَالُواْ سَمِعۡنَا وَأَطَعۡنَا وَٱسۡمَعۡ وَٱنظُرۡنَا لَكَانَ خَيۡرࣰ ا لَّهُمۡ وَأَقۡوَمَ وَلَٰكِن لَّعَنَهُمُ ٱللَّهُ بِكُفۡرِهِمۡ فَلَا يُؤۡمِنُونَ إِلَّا قَلِيلࣰ ا
4:46.en: Some of those who are Jews change words from their context and say: "We hear and disobey; hear thou as one who heareth not" and "Listen to us!" distorting with their tongues and slandering religion. If they had said: "We hear and we obey: hear thou, and look at us" it had been better for them, and more upright. But Allah hath cursed them for their disbelief, so they believe not, save a few

46:9.ar: قُلۡ مَا كُنتُ بِدۡعࣰ ا مِّنَ ٱلرُّسُلِ وَمَآ أَدۡرِي مَا يُفۡعَلُ بِي وَلَا بِكُمۡۖ إِنۡ أَتَّبِعُ إِلَّا مَا يُوحَىٰٓ إِلَيَّ وَمَآ أَنَا۠ إِلَّا نَذِيرࣱ مُّبِينࣱ‏
46:9.en: Say: I am no new thing among the messengers (of Allah), nor know I what will be done with me or with you. I do but follow that which is inspired in me, and I am but a plain warner

2:228.ar: وَٱلۡمُطَلَّقَٰتُ يَتَرَبَّصۡنَ بِأَنفُسِهِنَّ ثَلَٰثَةَ قُرُوٓءࣲۚ وَلَا يَحِلُّ لَهُنَّ أَن يَكۡتُمۡنَ مَا خَلَقَ ٱللَّهُ فِيٓ أَرۡحَامِهِنَّ إِن كُنَّ يُؤۡمِنَّ بِٱللَّهِ وَٱلۡيَوۡمِ ٱلۡأٓخِرِۚ وَبُعُولَتُهُنَّ أَحَقُّ بِرَدِّهِنَّ فِي ذَٰلِكَ إِنۡ أَرَادُوٓاْ إِصۡلَٰحࣰ اۚ وَلَهُنَّ مِثۡلُ ٱلَّذِي عَلَيۡهِنَّ بِٱلۡمَعۡرُوفِۚ وَلِلرِّجَالِ عَلَيۡهِنَّ دَرَجَةࣱۗ وَٱللَّهُ عَزِيزٌ حَكِيمٌ
2:228.en: Women who are divorced shall wait, keeping themselves apart, three (monthly) courses. And it is not lawful for them that they should conceal that which Allah hath created in their wombs if they are believers in Allah and the Last Day. And their husbands would do better to take them back in that case if they desire a reconciliation. And they (women) have rights similar to those (of men) over them in kindness, and men are a degree above them. Allah is Mighty, Wise
